Description: The physical trust boundary representing the local smart device hardware installed in the home.
(Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems) Hardware sensors collecting real-time temperature, humidity, and air quality data.
Internal software component that collects and normalizes raw readings from the sensors before storage.
Temporary on-device storage (cache/buffer) ensuring data availability for local commands or when offline.
The communication module responsible for securely uploading telemetry to the cloud and receiving updates.
The decision logic engine that translates user inputs or cloud insights into physical control signals.
The trust boundary representing the remote server infrastructure (likely AWS based on component names).
The cloud ingress point (likely an IoT Broker) that ingests high-volume telemetry from many devices.
Scalable cloud object storage used to persist historical sensor data and system logs.
Machine learning service that analyzes historical data to generate predictive comfort models and efficiency insights.
The interface layer allowing external apps, voice assistants, and the device itself to exchange data and commands.
Third-party external platforms (e.g., Alexa, Google Assistant) allowing voice control of the system.
The remote user interface allowing the human user to monitor and control the system via smartphone or browser.
The end-user interacting with the system via touch, voice, or mobile apps.
(Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning) The physical external system controlled by the device to regulate temperature.
The physical external appliance controlled by the device to filter air particulates.
The local physical interface allowing the user to view status and manually adjust settings.
